records.c: Character patterns $00-$3F, 64 eight-byte glyphs. The story renderer maps input codes $20-$3F to successive pairs here; the digits $30-$39 select pairs $20/$21 through $32/$33.

Character patterns $40-$75, 54 eight-byte glyphs. The story renderer maps @ to $40/$41 and letters A-Z or a-z to pairs $42/$43 through $74/$75, storing the even and odd codes in two successive screen rows.

Character-set bytes for the second through eighth rows of code $44 and all eight rows of codes $45–$75. The story renderer maps B through Z to the paired codes $44/$45 through $74/$75, so these patterns form those letters in the title's character-mode band. Code $44's first byte is at $2220.
Sprite 0: 63 bitmap bytes in 21 rows of three and one byte outside the bitmap, selected by pointer $A0. The setup places this white layer at the upper left position in the title sprite group.

Sixteen 40-byte rows of screen-matrix colours for the title bitmap. The routine at $14DB copies these 640 bytes to $6000–$627F, alongside the bitmap source at $6400–$77FF. Each matrix byte supplies two colours for its eight-byte bitmap cell.
Matrix source offsets $100–$17F. The copy at $14DB writes these 128 bytes to $6100–$617F as part of the 640-byte title picture matrix; each byte supplies two colours for one bitmap cell.
Matrix source offsets $180–$27F. The copy at $14DB writes these 256 bytes to $6180–$627F as part of the 640-byte title picture matrix; each byte supplies two colours for one bitmap cell.
The byte $0F supplies colour RAM for the title picture. The copy routine at $14DB reads it and writes it to $D800,X and $D840,X while preparing the display.

Thirty-six space-padded 40-byte rows name the game staff, music credits, developer, publisher and game title, ending with a prompt to press a key. The zero at $C7A0 terminates the text passed to the story renderer at $1924.

Continuation of the title's 40-byte credit rows at $C200: the last 16 bytes of row 25 and all of rows 26 through 34. The text includes the game title, copyright credit and key prompt, padded with spaces. The story renderer reads the rows from $C200.
Final 40-byte row of spaces in the title credits. The zero at $C7A0 immediately after it terminates the text sequence read by the story renderer.

Use A to select a seven-byte record at $EB5C: one accumulator increment and three little-endian pointers. Clear the three $24-byte channel state blocks, initialize their pointers and counters from the selected record, clear SID registers, and enable the channel update flags.

Read two bytes from the stream pointer $F0/$F1 into $E0C5/$E0C6,X, then jump to $E28F, which initializes the sequence offset and reads its first pointer. The command table at $E252 selects this entry.

Add the indexed offset at $E0C7/$E0C8,X to the sequence base at $E0C5/$E0C6,X and place the result in $F0/$F1. Advance the offset by 2, including any carry from the preceding high-byte addition. If the two bytes at that address are zero, $E28F restores the base and resets the offset to 2. Read the chosen little-endian pointer into $F0/$F1 and jump to $E3B7. How this entry is reached remains open.
Clear $E0D4,X, $E0D5,X and $E0DA,X, then jump to $E3CE. The command table at $E226 selects this entry.
Clear $E0DA,X and jump to $E3CE. Entry 21 of the command table selects this path.
Copy one byte from the stream pointer $F0/$F1 into the immediate operand at $E464, advance the stream pointer by one with carry and jump to $E3B7. Entry 20 of the command table selects this path.

Copy one byte from the stream pointer $F0/$F1 into $E0E5,X, advance the stream pointer by one with carry and jump to $E3B7. Entry 23 of the command table selects this path; the frequency routine adds $E0E5,X to its selected pitch.
Copy three bytes from the sound stream into indexed voice state at $E0DF-$E0E1, advance the stream pointer by three, set $E0E2 to one, and continue reading commands.
Select $80 for the indexed voice's $E0E3 state, then continue reading commands. The following entry points select $40, $20 or $10 instead.
Clear two indexed voice state bytes, take the next stream byte into $E0D9, advance the pointer and continue reading commands.

Set bit $20 in the indexed voice's $E0C2 state, clear $E0C9 and $E0CA, and copy three stream bytes to $E0CE-$E0D0. The $E341 entry sets bit $04 instead. Both advance the pointer by three and continue reading.
Copy two stream bytes to the indexed voice's $E0DC and $E0DB state, copy the second to $E0DD, advance the pointer by two, and set $E0DE to $40.
Clear the indexed voice's $E0DE state and continue reading the stream.
Set the low two bits of the indexed voice's $E0C2 state and continue reading the stream.

Count down the indexed voice's delay. When it expires, read its byte stream: values below $80 set the next value and reload the delay, $80-$BF dispatch through the command table, and higher values change stream parameters before reading again. Save the advanced pointer when a value is accepted.

Read one byte through $F0/$F1 and advance that pointer with carry. For a byte below $80, set $E0DA,X to 1, store the byte at $E0D3,X, copy $E0D2,X to $E0D1,X, save the updated stream pointer in $E0C3/$E0C4,X and return. Bytes $80–$BF dispatch through $E42C; bytes $C0–$FF take the paths beginning at $E3E0.

For input $C0–$CF, the additions at $E3E4/$E3E8/$E3EC yield an index from 0 to 15. Use it to read low/high bytes from the tables at $E668/$E676 into $E0CB/$E0CC,X, clear $E0CD,X, set bit $10 of $E0C2,X and read another stream byte. The known tables each have 14 entries; this path does not check the index. Inputs $D0–$DF branch to $E411, and $E0–$FF branch to $E40A.
The preceding addition leaves carry set and A in $00–$1F for input $E0–$FF. Add that carry, store 1–32 at $E0D2,X and return to $E3B7 to read another stream byte.
Read two bytes through $F0/$F1 into $E0D4,X and $E0D5,X, advance the stream pointer by two with carry and jump to $E3B7. The high-byte decoder selects this path for input $D0–$DF.

Double an input in $80–$BF and use the resulting byte as an offset into the little-endian table at $E226. Copy the selected pair into the jump operand at $E43B/$E43C and jump through it. The documented table has 24 entries; this path does not check that the offset lies within them.

For the channel selected by X, read a byte from the stream addressed by $E0CB/$E0CC plus $E0CD. A byte with bit 7 set resets the stream offset to $FF and has that bit cleared. Add $E0D3, the global offset at $E464 and $E0E5; use the result to select a little-endian frequency from $E5C2. The continuation at $E464 applies the channel's optional frequency and pulse adjustments and stores the resulting SID values in its state block.

Immediate operand of the ADC at $E463. Initialization clears it; a sound-stream command at $E2C7 replaces it. The same routine then adds the channel byte at $E0E5, looks up a two-byte frequency and applies enabled pitch and pulse-width adjustments before storing the channel's frequency at $E0D6/$E0D7 and pulse width at $E0D8/$E0D9.

Toggle bit 0 of $E0C2,X. Depending on bits $24 and a counter at $E0D0,X, update a two-byte accumulator at $E0C9/$E0CA,X and add it to or subtract it from the frequency at $F0/$F1. The routine then moves the two-byte value at $E0D8/$E0D9,X between limits under control of $E0E2,X. Finally it stores the resulting frequency in $E0D6/$E0D7,X and a value derived from $E0E3,X in $E0E4,X.

The first 82 little-endian values in the sound driver's frequency lookup. The driver doubles its index and reads a pair at $E46C and $E471; the sampled story, Broadway and outcome selections read within this portion. The table's full extent remains open.
The high byte of the first frequency value; the little-endian pairs begin one byte earlier at $E5C2 and continue through $E665.

Continuation of the little-endian frequency values starting at $E5C2. This byte is the high byte of entry 32; $E604–$E665 contain entries 33 through 81. The reader at $E46C/$E471 doubles its index and reads the low and high bytes.
Fourteen low bytes of pointers selected by a stream command at $E3EF; the corresponding high bytes start at $E676.
Fourteen high bytes paired with the low bytes at $E668, read by the command at $E3F5. The pointed-to data is not yet classified.

Update the shared modulation state, then call each active voice's effect routine according to the three flags at $E12F-$E131.

Update the first voice's timed effect. When its remaining count reaches zero, clear its active flag and envelope registers and set its completion flag. Otherwise count down the effect, periodically reload its frequency and add or subtract its configured frequency step before writing SID voice 1.
Update the second voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 2.
Update the third voice's timed effect: clear its flag and envelope on expiry, otherwise count down, reload and step its frequency and write SID voice 3.
